facts.d: The Constitution's third tier of ministerial office was routinely used until the 1970s and 1980s. No Deputy Minister features in current Union practice — the rank survives on paper while the ministry is built entirely from Cabinet Ministers and Ministers of State.

facts.t: India has no ministerial code; Britain revises its own
facts.d: The United Kingdom's Ministerial Code covers conflicts of interest, use of public resources and relations with the civil service. India's Transaction of Business Rules regulate procedure only. The Second ARC recommended a code of ethics — it has never been implemented.

facts.t: Ambedkar resigned rather than dissent from inside
facts.d: He left the Cabinet in 1953 over the Hindu Code Bill. That is the ethical logic of collective responsibility: a minister who cannot defend a decision resigns rather than opposing it while in office — a convention Britain still honours and India largely does not.

bank.q: With reference to the constitutional position of ministers, consider the following statements:
s: The 42nd Amendment made ministerial advice binding on the President.
The 44th Amendment permits the President one reconsideration.
The 91st Amendment capped the Council of Ministers at 15% of Lok Sabha strength.
bank.e: All three are correct, and together they trace how ministerial authority was consolidated and then bounded.

bank.q: Bimolangshu Roy v. State of Assam (2017) struck down Parliamentary Secretary posts as violating:
bank.e: Article 164(1A), the state-level cap on ministry size — such posts effectively enlarged the ministry beyond the permitted limit.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about ministerial ranks?
o: A Minister of State with independent charge heads a ministry
A Minister of State with independent charge attends all Cabinet meetings by right
Deputy Ministers do not attend Cabinet
Parliamentary Secretaries find no mention in the Constitution
bank.e: They attend only when invited. Full attendance with voting rights belongs to Cabinet Ministers alone.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (holding on collective responsibility):
pairs: 1. Two dimensions — unified policy support and shared success or failure
2. Ministers must defend Cabinet decisions inside and outside Parliament
3. A minister's personal remarks do not bind the government
4. Fixed tenure and a Civil Services Board
bank.e: R. K. Jain on the duty to defend, S. P. Anand on personal remarks, Common Cause on the two dimensions, and T. S. R. Subramanian on civil service reform.

bank.as: Individual ministerial responsibility is weaker in India than in the United Kingdom.
bank.rs: British ministers have resigned for departmental failures without personal involvement, as in the Crichel Down affair.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. India saw no preemptive resignations over 2G, the Commonwealth Games or the Coal allocations.

bank.q: With reference to the 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2025, consider the following:
s: It would apply to the Prime Minister as well as other ministers.
The trigger is detention for thirty consecutive days on allegation of an offence punishable with five years or more.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The trigger is detention, not conviction — which is the principal objection raised against it on the presumption of innocence.

bank.q: Under the 130th Amendment Bill, if removal does not occur, the office ceases automatically on:
bank.e: The 31st day. Re-appointment is permitted once the person is released.

bank.q: All of the following are identified as problems with Indian ministers EXCEPT:
o: Absence of a dedicated conflict-of-interest law
No constitutional requirement of subject expertise
A statutory bar on appointing persons with declared criminal cases
Post-retirement sinecures creating a revolving door
bank.e: No such bar exists. PUCL v. UoI merely observed that Prime Ministers and Chief Ministers should avoid persons with serious criminal antecedents.

bank.q: The minimum age to be a minister drawn from the Rajya Sabha is:
bank.e: Thirty, matching Rajya Sabha eligibility. It is twenty-five for a minister drawn from the Lok Sabha.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about Groups of Ministers:
s: Empowered Groups of Ministers carry financial and executive powers.
More than twenty-five Groups of Ministers were active by 2013.
They strengthened individual accountability by clearly assigning responsibility.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Critics argued they diffused accountability — a minister could always point to the Group.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a proposed reform?
o: A Ministerial Accountability Act defining resignation triggers
A fixed calendar of at least 100 sitting days a year
Automatic dissolution of Groups of Ministers that do not report within six months
Removing the 15% cap on ministry size
bank.e: The debate concerns whether the cap is too low for modern governance, but no proposal seeks its removal.

bank.as: The Cabinet is meant to be accountable to Parliament but in practice controls it.
bank.rs: Government dominance over the Business Advisory Committee lets Bills pass without standing committee scrutiny.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the fusion that makes the system responsive is the same fusion that erodes its scrutiny.
